content: Ciprofloxacin and dexamethasone are combined in a sterile otic suspension known as CIPRODEX® Otic. This medication is used to treat bacterial infections of the ear, specifically acute otitis externa (commonly referred to as swimmer's ear) and acute otitis media with tympanostomy tubes in patients aged six months and older. The active ingredients include ciprofloxacin, a broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibiotic, and dexamethasone, a corticosteroid with anti-inflammatory properties. Indications and Dosage For acute otitis externa, the recommended dosage is four drops into the affected ear twice daily for seven days. For acute otitis media with tympanostomy tubes, the same dosage regimen applies. The suspension should be warmed by holding the bottle in the hand for one to two minutes before administration to prevent dizziness caused by the instillation of a cold solution. Patients should lie with the affected ear upward, and the tragus should be pumped five times to facilitate penetration of the drops into the middle ear. This position should be maintained for 60 seconds. Any unused portion of the medication should be discarded after the therapy is completed. Contraindications CIPRODEX® Otic is contraindicated in patients with a history of hypersensitivity to ciprofloxacin, other quinolones, dexamethasone, or any of the components of the medication. It should not be used in cases of viral infections of the external ear canal, such as herpes simplex. Warnings and Precautions This product is for otic use only and is not approved for ophthalmic use or injection. It should be discontinued immediately if a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity occurs. Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported with systemic quinolones, sometimes after the first dose. Emergency treatment may be required in such cases. The use of this product may lead to the overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms, including yeast and fungi. If the infection does not improve after one week of treatment, cultures should be obtained to guide further therapy. Persistent otorrhea or recurrent episodes of otorrhea within six months warrant further evaluation to rule out underlying conditions such as cholesteatoma, foreign body, or tumor. Systemic administration of quinolones at high doses has been associated with cartilage lesions and arthropathy in immature animals. However, studies in guinea pigs dosed in the middle ear with CIPRODEX® Otic for one month showed no drug-related structural or functional changes in cochlear hair cells or ossicles. No local irritation was observed when the product was applied topically to the rabbit eye. Adverse Reactions In clinical trials, the most common adverse reactions included ear discomfort, otalgia, pruritus of the skin and ear, and abnormal taste. Rare adverse events included tympanostomy tube blockage, tinnitus, oral moniliasis, dizziness, and erythema. If any of these side effects persist or worsen, patients should contact their healthcare provider. Allergic reactions require immediate discontinuation of the product and consultation with a physician. Use in Specific Populations Pregnancy: CIPRODEX® Otic is classified as Pregnancy Category C. Animal studies have not shown evidence of harm to the fetus with ciprofloxacin, but corticosteroids are generally teratogenic in laboratory animals at low doses. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women, so caution is advised. Nursing Mothers: Ciprofloxacin and corticosteroids may appear in breast milk following oral administration. The potential for adverse effects in nursing infants, such as growth suppression or interference with endogenous corticosteroid production, should be considered. A decision should be made to discontinue nursing or the drug, taking into account its importance to the mother. Pediatric Use: Safety and efficacy have been established in patients aged six months and older. No data are available for patients younger than six months, but there are no known safety concerns that would preclude its use in this population. Geriatric Use: There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of CIPRODEX® Otic in geriatric patients. Administration and Monitoring The suspension should be shaken well before use. Patients should follow the prescribed dosing schedule and complete the full course of therapy, even if symptoms improve, to prevent recurrence of the infection. If a dose is missed, it should be administered as soon as possible unless it is almost time for the next dose. Double dosing is not recommended. Pharmacology Ciprofloxacin acts by inhibiting bacterial DNA gyrase, an enzyme essential for DNA synthesis, leading to bacterial cell death. Dexamethasone reduces inflammation associated with bacterial infections. Ciprofloxacin has in vitro activity against a wide range of gram-positive and gram-negative microorganisms, including Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Storage CIPRODEX® Otic should be stored at controlled room temperature (15°C to 30°C or 59°F to 86°F). It should be protected from light and not frozen. Important Patient Information Patients should avoid getting the infected ear(s) wet during bathing and should refrain from swimming unless instructed otherwise by their doctor. If the infection does not improve after one week or if there are recurrent episodes of drainage, further medical evaluation is recommended. This medication is available only by prescription and should not be used if outdated. If accidentally swallowed or overdosed, medical attention should be sought immediately. Alcohol Interaction There is no established interaction between alcohol and CIPRODEX® Otic. Patients should consult their doctor regarding alcohol consumption while using this medication. Brand Name CIPRODEX® Otic is the brand name for this combination product.
